pick.name: Nurix Therapeutics, Inc.
pick.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on operating margin trend, growth acceleration, revenue growth, trailing year — revenue +738.8% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

signalsDropped.why: gross profit or total assets is not reported

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield

pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below -79.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $19.77 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-09-30, 15 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-15.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-28) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set
sources.prices: Massive (Polygon.io) grouped daily bars, splits and dividends

stories.title: Coastal homes burn as hot winds fuel California fires
stories.excerpt: High winds are fueling a fast-moving fire that has burned homes in Southern California. Flames engulfed expensive coastal properties and prompted thousands to evacuate.
stories.lead:
A fast-moving fire fueled by high winds burned at least six homes in Southern California on Friday, engulfing expensive coastal properties and prompting thousands to evacuate.

Black smoke — visible from miles away — billowed over tennis courts and swimming pools while firefighters doused blazing homes in San Juan Capistrano in Orange County. Some homeowners sprayed water on their properties before heeding evacuation orders.

Two firefighters were taken to the hospital with heat-related injuries, officials said. Authorities have not said how the blaze, which was less than a square mile as of Friday evening, started.

stories.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
stories.excerpt: The US president temporarily ends many restrictions on Moscow recently passed by Congress over "national security" concerns.
stories.lead:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by Trump in September.

But the US president issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US "national interest", prompting a backlash from US lawmakers.

stories.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
stories.excerpt: The 16-year-old suspect previously attended the primary school and had targeted a special educational needs classroom, police say.
stories.lead:
An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and attempted to disarm a teenager who opened fire on a special educational needs class.

As she tried to wrestle a shotgun off him on the floor of the classroom - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander armed with a pistol ran inside and killed the teen.

The bystander, a father of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend at lunchtime on Thursday when he saw the suspect firing in the school's car park and then shooting through a window to enter.

stories.title: Amid talk of public execution, public opinion on death penalty is split
stories.excerpt: A majority of Americans support the death penalty for people convicted of murder, but support becomes more divided when questions vary.
stories.lead:
U.S. public sentiment about the death penalty has come to the forefront after President Trump gave his blessing, then backtracked, to livestreaming an execution via firing squad.

That planned execution comes after two botched Tennessee lethal injections this year, where the state struggled to find veins to administer death-inducing drugs to Christa Pike and Tony Carruthers.

Speaking at a press conference a day after Pike's failed execution, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee said Tennesseans were disappointed about what happened.

stories.title: Tritons Fall to Gauchos at Home
stories.excerpt: The UC San Diego men's water polo team was defeated by UC Santa Barbara, 14-8, Friday in a Big West match-up at Canyonview Aquatic Center.
stories.lead:
With the loss, the eighth-ranked Tritons fell to 12-6 overall and 1-1 in the conference. The 14th-ranked Gauchos improved to 19-9 on the season and 1-1 in Big West action.

Triton junior Christian Hammonds scored his seventh hat trick of the season, finding the back of the net three times. He also had an assist and three steals. Sophomore Jackson Boettner and freshman Bryan Shapirshteyn contributed two goals apiece.

stories.title: Water Polo Retains Judge Cup with 24-10 Win over Iona
stories.excerpt: Water polo defeats Iona, 24-10.
stories.lead:
Bronx, N.Y. – Five members of the Judge family played water polo for Iona University. Only two, the patriarch, Francis, and Chris, donned a Fordham maroon cap in their careers. Tonight the Ram alumni have bragging rights as Fordham defeated Iona, 24-10, in the Messmore Aquatics Center in the annual battle for the Judge Cup.

With the win, Fordham improves to 16-1 on the season while Iona falls to 6-16.

Fordham was led by sophomore Diego Tresa, who netted four goals, while freshmen Oktavian Veklyuk, Petar Kulas, and Karlo Dragosevic each added three goals.
